keyAndScale.modalCharacter: Playful contrast between a dry, off-beat B Aeolian reggae-rock verse and a sun-drenched D Ionian relative-major chorus
keyAndScale.relativeMinor: B minor is the relative minor of D major

mainProgression.progressionDescription: Infectious reggae-pop loop in B minor using the subtonic A major and submediant G major to create a buoyant, circular travelogue groove.

sectionProgressions.section: Intro & Verse ('Traveling in a fried-out Kombi')
sectionProgressions.description: Crisp reggae upstroke skank on beats 2-and and 4-and over a bouncy bassline

sectionProgressions.section: Chorus ('Can't you hear, can't you hear the thunder?')
sectionProgressions.description: Replaces the opening Bm chord with its relative major D, instantly lifting the hook into a stadium singalong
Famous B minor pentatonic/Aeolian flute motif arranged for lead guitar
B natural minor flute-hook melody arranged on strings 1 to 3

harmonicFunction: Bm (i) - Minor tonic establishing the quirky, deadpan verse storytelling
D (bIII / Relative I) - Relative major tonic brightening the first beat of every chorus line
A (bVII) - Subtonic chord providing constant rhythmic bounce back to Bm or D
G (bVI) - Submediant chord pairing with A for the classic bVI-bVII turnaround at the end of every two-bar phrase

techniques.name: Reggae-Pop Offbeat Skank & Relative Major Chorus Lift
techniques.description: Tight, staccato offbeat barre-chord chops in the verse paired with open, ringing power/open chords in the chorus.

sequence: Mute strings on the downbeats (1, 2, 3, 4) and strike crisp upstrokes on the '&' of beats during the verse
Release fretting-hand pressure immediately after each upstroke to get a dry, percussive chop
Switch the first chord of the loop from Bm to open D major when the chorus hits
Play the G to A turnaround on beats 3 and 4 of every second bar
tips: For the verse reggae chop, use compact 3- or 4-string barre shapes on the top strings so every chord cuts cleanly
Count '1 & 2 & 3 & 4 &' out loud and accent the '&' syllables to lock into Colin Hay's rhythm
In the chorus, let the open D major chord ring out fully to contrast with the clipped verse

techniques.name: Ron Strykert Strat Stabs & 7th-Position Flute Doubling
techniques.description: Playing lead guitarist Ron Strykert's funky, rhythmic Strat fills and transcribing Greg Ham's famous B Aeolian hook into 7th-position lead guitar lines with crisp single-coil quack.

notes: 7th position B minor pentatonic and Aeolian notes (strings 1-4, frets 7-10)
Crisp staccato picking on beat subdivisions
Out-of-phase pickup cluck (Strat position 2 or 4)
Subtle quarter-note delay and light compression
sequence: Anchor your fretting hand in 7th position across strings 1 to 4
Double the flute riff with punchy downstrokes on the 9th fret D and 7th fret B
Add syncopated double-stop stabs between vocal lines
Accentuate the dynamic drop into the verse after the flute hook
tips: Ron Strykert used a Fender Stratocaster in the in-between pickup position into a Roland Jazz Chorus for razor-sharp clarity
Keep notes strictly staccato—do not let open strings ring into the single-note lines
Slight palm muting on the 4th string adds punch to the low B notes

sections.name: Intro Flute Hook & Atmospheric Skank
sections.description: The immortal opening hook featuring Greg Ham's iconic flute theme transcribed for 7th-position electric guitar over the subtle reggae skank.
notes: Play in 7th position with index finger barring frets 7 on strings 1 to 3
Use crisp staccato articulation to emulate the wooden flute attack
Target root B on string 4 fret 9 and string 1 fret 7

sections.name: Verse 1 Reggae Storytelling Skank
sections.description: Clipped, bouncy offbeat chords over the two-bar Bm - A - Bm - G - A groove supporting Colin Hay's legendary lyrics.
notes: Focus on the upper four strings for a bright, reggae-influenced chop
Release finger pressure right after striking to stop the chord from ringing
Nail the quick G to A change in the second bar on beats 3 and 4

sections.name: Pre-Chorus Build & Percussive Chops
sections.description: The quick two-bar transition ('He just smiled and gave me a Vegemite sandwich') building toward the major-key explosion.
notes: Keep the stabs tight and synchronized with Jerry Speiser's hi-hat
Emphasize the punch on the G major chord
Leave a micro-beat of silence before striking the chorus D major downbeat

sections.name: Chorus Stadium Lift ('Land Down Under')
sections.description: Substituting D major for the first Bm chord transforms the minor verse loop into an unforgettable major-key anthem singalong.
notes: Hit the open D major chord strongly on beat 1 of bar 1
Notice how bars 1 and 2 still end with the exact same G to A turnaround
Keep the 107 BPM groove buoyant and relaxed

sections.name: Ron Strykert Guitar Break & Instrumental Solo
sections.description: Ron Strykert's sharp Stratocaster lead lines dancing over the Bm - A - Bm - G - A progression in the instrumental interlude.
notes: Crisp 7th position phrasing blending B minor pentatonic with natural minor color
Short, biting pick attack on single-coil bridge/middle pickup
Target the tonic B (7th fret high E) on strong beat accents

sections.name: Outro Chorus & Reggae Jam Fade
sections.description: The exuberant outro where the band jams on the chorus progression with improvising vocal shouts, flute counter-melodies, and driving guitar chops.
notes: Alternate between ringing D power chords and punchy upstroke skanks
Lock into John Rees's bouncing bass groove
Gradually soften dynamics into the final studio fade

guitar.recommended: Fender Telecaster or Fender Stratocaster (Colin Hay & Ron Strykert)
alternatives: Maton Acoustic (for Colin Hay unplugged style)
guitar.pickup: Bridge and middle single-coil combination for snappy new-wave cluck

amp.recommended: Roland JC-120 or Fender Twin Reverb

effects.distortion: Light overdrive on chorus power chords
effects.delay: Short slapback or quarter-note dub echo
effects.other: Compressor pedal for even, percussive upstroke volume

beginner.title: Four-Chord Loop & Simplified Bm
steps: Learn D, A, G, and the 4-string Bm triad (X-X-4-4-3-2)
Practice the two-bar verse loop (Bm - A | Bm - G - A) with simple downstrokes
Switch the first Bm to D major for the chorus
Play through the full song at 107 BPM

intermediate.title: Reggae Upstroke Skank & Full Barre Chords
steps: Master the full 5-string Bm barre chord (X-2-4-4-3-2)
Play the verse using muted downbeats and staccato upstrokes on the '&' counts
Learn the B minor flute melody on the upper strings

advanced.title: Loop-Pedal Arrangement (Rhythm + Flute Lead)
steps: Lay down the reggae rhythm loop and perform the flute hook live over the top
Incorporate Ron Strykert's syncopated single-note muted funk-reggae lines
Perform Colin Hay's dynamic solo-acoustic storytelling arrangement

commonMistakes: Strumming heavy on beats 1 and 3 in the verse instead of accenting the offbeats
Forgetting that the second bar of every phrase has a faster harmonic rhythm (Bm for 2 beats, then G and A for 1 beat each)
Failing to mute the low E string on the Bm barre chord
practiceRoutine: 3 minutes: Bm → A → G chord transition drill
4 minutes: Offbeat upstroke skank exercise with fretting-hand muting at 90 BPM
4 minutes: Flute hook lead melody practice in 7th position
4 minutes: Full song playthrough at 107 BPM
focusAreas: Crisp fretting-hand muting for reggae upstrokes
Seamless switch between the B minor verse and D major chorus
Accurate timing on the G-A bar-2 turnaround
metronomeWork: Set metronome to 90 BPM and treat clicks as beats 2 and 4
Bring tempo up to 107 BPM while keeping upstrokes razor-sharp
Practice transitioning between the rhythm skank and the single-note flute lead
